drivers.reason: Use lighter neighbouring displays for temporary review cohorts below the established family story. The review label follows each cohort; co-location does not imply a shared region or lineage.

drivers.connection: Vraj → Rama → Kashi along adjacent cases
drivers.reason: Mirabai and the Vraj Ramanandis form the Vraj side. Ravidas at 78 leads toward Tulsidas / Rama at 36, then Kabir / Kashi at 29. Trailanga at 76 and Kashi / ascetic families at 28 continue the same face of the island.

drivers.reason: Goraknath / Nath context in 40, Nivrittinath contextual interpretation across 40–41, Dnyaneshwar in 41, then the Varkari run 42–45. No Nivrittinath relic record is invented.

drivers.reason: Expanded Datta island 3 / 80–82; intact Meher Baba and Sai group in 4. They are nearby across the passage, not a same-face contiguous run.

drivers.connection: Kriya together; Himalayan masters toward the cave
drivers.reason: Kriya uses the first four contiguous stations from 5; Sivananda / Tapovan / Chinmayananda follow at 73 / 25; the other Himalayan masters finish at 26 / 37, with Haidakhan Babaji at 37.

drivers.connection: Andhra Avadhuta / Datta families toward the Datta island
drivers.reason: Andhra families move down the outer island face to 21 / 22 / 74. This is a shorter visitor approach to the Datta island, not same-face adjacency to it.

drivers.connection: Neem Karoli Baba in the northern setting
drivers.reason: Neem Karoli Baba is anchored at 26 alongside other distinct northern saints, with Haidakhan Babaji at 37. Nearby placement does not assert a guru–disciple relationship.

drivers.connection: South–West hinge at the western approach
drivers.reason: The three remain together in 14, at the southern wall end nearest the western entrance-room approach. Ramana’s intact group uses 19 / 20, facing the southern wall displays. These are visitor-route and facing connections, not same-face adjacency to the western island.

drivers.connection: Western overflow with intact Secondary groups
drivers.reason: Use 39 for intact western family groups rather than treating it as empty reserve. The complete remaining western inventory still creates pressure; the region’s internal envelopes need balancing before physical execution.

drivers.connection: Eastern families beside Ramakrishna
drivers.reason: Other eastern families use 51 and 56. The immediate Ramakrishna group stays together at 57; 56 becomes a neighbouring teaching-family display instead of an exclusive Ramakrishna reserve.

drivers.connection: Western regional cohorts around preserved family anchors
drivers.reason: Use lighter western cases for distinct lower-priority Gujarati / Maharashtra / source-context cohorts while retaining every named Primary / Secondary placement. Sai–Meher 4 receives no additional unrelated cohorts. This is regional co-location, not a new guru or tradition claim.

drivers.connection: Vraj traditions along 6–11

tradeoffs: 12 receives the complete Devraha display grouping from 11: the Primary record, Madhusudan, Ayodhya Das, Devra Hansa and the separate Dev Raha record. The source identities remain separate.
15 receives Shivaprabhakara and his existing display companion from 17, together with source-associated Kerala saints from 17 / 20 and the reviewed Chattampi identification.
72 receives the Karnataka / Hubli–Mugalkhod source grouping from 20, including Yellaling and Yedehalli Ajji together. This keeps the left-hand neighbourhood southern.
All lower identity-review cohorts keep their case assignments and labels. Their host region is not attributed to them.

Principal anchors and Secondary families receive upper / readable positions; other regional companions retain their existing tiers. Actual shelf positions and physical fit remain for on-site confirmation.
